endorsements.name: Sergey Shekyan
endorsements.label: Hacking with WebSockets
endorsements.description: HTML5 isn't just for watching videos on your iPad. Its features may be the target of a security attack as much as they may be used to improve an attack. Vulnerabilities like XSS have been around since the web's beginning, but exploiting them has become increasingly sophisticated. HTML5 features like WebSockets are part of the framework for controlling browsers compromised by XSS.
endorsements.subtitle: Black Hat Usa 2012

endorsements.name: Sergey Shekyan
endorsements.label: Dissecting CSRF Attacks & Countermeasures
endorsements.description: Cross Site Request Forgery (CSRF) remains a significant threat to web apps and user data. Current countermeasures like request nonces can be cumbersome to deploy correctly and difficult to apply to a site retroactively. Detecting these vulns with automated tools can be equally difficult to do accurately.
endorsements.subtitle: Black Hat Usa 2013
